seo_description: Meet Samuel Bahago Gabriel, a geospatial analyst and geoscience professional working across GIS, remote sensing, hydrology and environmental planning.

hero.heading: Geoscience training.
hero.intro: I am a geospatial analyst who combines earth-science understanding, spatial data and modelling to help explain landscapes and support practical decisions.

story.heading: From geology to decision-ready geography.
story.photo_alt: Samuel Bahago Gabriel during an ACReSAL stakeholder engagement
paragraphs: My background in Geology and Mineral Resources Engineering shaped the way I read landscapes. GIS gave me the tools to connect terrain, water, land use, infrastructure and communities within one analytical framework.

Since beginning my GIS career in 2019, I have worked on catchment-management programmes, dam and irrigation studies, flood-risk assessments, groundwater investigations, mining-impact studies and environmental baselines. At MECON Services Ltd., I support multidisciplinary teams from early data preparation and fieldwork through analysis, cartography and technical reporting.
I am especially interested in work where spatial evidence can improve climate resilience, water-resource management and environmental planning in Nigeria and across Africa.

values.heading: Analytical rigour with practical purpose.
values.intro: Strong GIS work should be technically sound, understandable and grounded in the place it represents.

items.title: Evidence first
items.text: I build conclusions from traceable datasets, appropriate methods and transparent assumptions.

items.title: Think in systems
items.text: Environmental problems connect terrain, water, land use, infrastructure and human activity.

items.title: Listen locally
items.text: Field observations and stakeholder knowledge make regional analysis more useful and realistic.

items.title: Communicate clearly
items.text: Maps and reports should help both technical teams and decision-makers understand what matters.

fieldwork.heading: Field engagement is part of the analysis.
fieldwork.text: For the Strategic Catchment Management Plans, I supported engagements and spatial data integration across the 19 Northern States and the FCT. Those conversations helped convert local experience and institutional priorities into mapped evidence.
